scope: Theorem 3.7 (Endpoint multilinear Kakeya) of the manuscript “The Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions” (preprints/The-Kakeya-maximal-conjecture-in-three-dimensions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 074 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 49cc52aa3de89f0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For j = 1, 2, 3, let Tj,a be finitely many infinite cylinders of radius one in R3, with unit axial directions vj,a. Suppose | det(v1,a1 , v2,a2 , v3,a3 )| ≥ θ > 0 for every (a1, a2, a3). For nonnegative weights ωj,a put µj = P a ωj,a1Tj,a and Mj = P a ωj,a. Then Z R3 (µ1µ2µ3)1/2 ≤ Cθ−1/2 (M1M2M3)1/2 . (3.10) In particular this holds for finite length-D tubes with no additional dependence on D.
